files.hooks/held-verdict/ask-kind.ts:
import type { EventResult } from 'claude-code'

/**
 * Names who asked, where no rule decided a verdict that holds: the classic
 * hook first, then the setting whose check asked, then the host it goes to.
 *
 * An ask that names none of the three holds by the ceiling an organization
 * set on the tool.
 *
 * @param held the ask in question
 * @returns `<event> hook's ask`, `<key> setting's ask`, `host's ask`, or
 *   `ask cap`
 */
export function askKind(held: EventResult<'tool.check'>) {
  const isHooked = held.hook !== undefined
  const isSet = held.setting !== undefined
  const isHosted = held.decider !== undefined

  return isHooked
    ? `${held.hook} hook's ask`
    : isSet
      ? `${held.setting} setting's ask`
      : isHosted
        ? `${held.decider}'s ask`
        : 'ask cap'
}
files.hooks/held-verdict/caught-answer.ts:
import type { EventResult, TraceEntry } from 'claude-code'

import Verdicts from './verdicts'

/**
 * What the `tool.check` hook's failure handler answers from the one run it
 * can read, the failed hook's last: that run's verdict, or a refusal.
 *
 * A verdict stands that no link that may hold a person's plugin rewrote
 * without tightening. A rewritten one, or none at all, met no rule or hook.
 *
 * @param last what that run settled on; undefined when it rejected
 * @param trace that run's `next.trace`
 * @returns the verdict the handler returns
 */
export function caughtAnswer(
  last: EventResult<'tool.check'> | undefined,
  trace: readonly TraceEntry<'tool.check'>[],
) {
  const isVouched =
    last !== undefined && Verdicts.rewrittenByUsers(trace).length === 0

  return isVouched ? last : Verdicts.UNCHECKED_DENY
}
files.hooks/held-verdict/held-kind.ts:
import type { EventResult } from 'claude-code'

import { askKind } from './ask-kind.js'

/**
 * What kind of thing held over a person's plugin, as the notice calls it:
 * `deny rule`, `ask rule`, `refusal`, or whose ask it was, else `ask cap`.
 *
 * A deny that names no rule is a refusal even when it names a hook: the hook
 * may only have asked, and something else refused. An ask that names nobody
 * holds by the ceiling an organization set on the tool.
 *
 * @param held the verdict that holds
 * @returns the kind
 */
export function heldKind(held: EventResult<'tool.check'>): string {
  const isRuled = held.rule !== undefined
  const isRefused = held.decision === 'deny'

  return isRuled
    ? `${held.decision} rule`
    : isRefused
      ? 'refusal'
      : askKind(held)
}
files.hooks/held-verdict/held-notice.ts:
import type { EventResult } from 'claude-code'

import { heldKind } from './held-kind.js'

/**
 * What a person reads, once for each plugin and kind in a session, when a
 * plugin they installed rewrote a verdict that holds over it.
 *
 * It names the option an administrator sets to let such plugins override.
 *
 * @param plugin the plugin's name, or its batch's, as the trace names it
 * @param tool the tool the call named
 * @param held the verdict that holds, naming the rule behind it if one is
 * @param attempt what the plugin did: answered looser, or the same reworded
 * @returns the line
 */
export function heldNotice(
  plugin: string,
  tool: string,
  held: EventResult<'tool.check'>,
  attempt: 'lift' | 'reword',
): string {
  const kind = heldKind(held)
  const article = kind.startsWith('a') ? 'an' : 'a'
  const changed =
    held.rule === undefined
      ? `${article} ${kind} from a ${tool} call`
      : `${article} ${kind} in your settings from a ${tool} call (${held.rule})`

  return (
    `${plugin} tried to ${attempt} ${changed}; the ${kind} holds over the ` +
    'plugins you install (allowModsToOverrideDenyRules)'
  )
}

 * A yes/no read off managed policy that fails closed: true (protect) when
 * the read rejects or deciding throws.

import type { Settings } from 'claude-code'

import { isPersonWritable } from './is-person-writable.js'
import { ownOption } from './own-option'

/**
 * Whether deny rules hold over the plugins a person installs: they do unless
 * an administrator's policy sets `allowModsToOverrideDenyRules` to `true`.
 *
 * Ask rules and classic hooks' answers hold or not with them. A value mistyped
 * (`"true"`, `1`) loosens nothing, and neither does the option in a policy the
 * person could have written (isPersonWritable).
 *
 * @param policy the managed settings, as `$.settings.read` answers them
 * @returns false only when the organization let a person's plugins override
 */
export const denyRulesHold = (policy: Settings) =>
  isPersonWritable(policy) ||
  ownOption(policy, 'allowModsToOverrideDenyRules') !== true

import type { Settings } from 'claude-code'

import { ownOption } from './own-option'

/**
 * Whether managed policy limits mods to the organization's: this plugin's
 * own option `allowManagedModsOnly` in managed settings.
 *
 * On unless absent or `false`: a value mistyped (`"true"`, `1`) still
 * locks, as the CLI's own managed locks read.
 *
 * @param policy the managed settings, as `$.settings.read` answers them
 * @returns true when the person's own mods are not to load
 */
export function isManagedModsOnly(policy: Settings) {
  const value = ownOption(policy, 'allowManagedModsOnly')

  return value !== undefined && value !== false
}

/**
 * Whether managed policy pins an environment variable: it sets the name
 * (pinnedNames), in any case (some systems read `Path` and `PATH` as one).

 * @param policy the managed settings, as `$.settings.read` answers them
 * @param name the variable a plugin would set or unset
 * @returns true when the organization set it

    pinned => pinned.toUpperCase() === name.toUpperCase(),

files.hooks/policy/names-org-tool.ts:
import type { Settings } from 'claude-code'

import { isServerFileUnreadable } from './managed-tools-restored/is-org-tool/is-server-file-unreadable'
import { orgNames } from './managed-tools-restored/is-org-tool/org-names'
import { toolPrefixOf } from './managed-tools-restored/is-org-tool/tool-prefix-of'
import { foldedName } from './managed-tools-restored/is-org-tool/tool-prefix-of/folded-name'

/**
 * Whether the tool a plugin registers would read as the organization's: it
 * is called `mcp__<plugin>__<tool>`, compared fold to fold with the prefix
 * of each server the policy names, each plugin it seats, and each seated
 * plugin's scope, which holds the servers its own manifest declares.
 *
 * So a plugin named as one of them in any case or with other separators, one
 * whose name and tool together spell a prefix, and one whose tool's own name
 * folds to nothing all count. A name of the organization's that folds to
 * nothing cannot be told from any name, and a server file that cannot be
 * read names nobody: every registration then reads as the organization's.
 * The plugin whose engine-recorded id managed enabledPlugins turn on keeps
 * its own name; an unreadable server file holds it all the same.
 *
 * @param policy the managed settings, as `$.settings.read` answers them
 * @param plugin the registering plugin's name
 * @param tool the tool's own name, as the plugin registers it
 * @param id the id the engine recorded for the registering plugin
 *           (`<name>@<source>`), where the mod heard its admission
 * @returns true when the tool would read as the organization's
 */
export function namesOrgTool(
  policy: Settings,
  plugin: string,
  tool: string,
  id?: string,
): boolean {
  const registered = `${foldedName(`mcp__${plugin}__${tool}`)}_`

  return (
    isServerFileUnreadable(policy) ||
    orgNames(policy, id).some(
      owner =>
        foldedName(owner) === '' || registered.startsWith(toolPrefixOf(owner)),
    )
  )
}

files.hooks/policy/pinned-names.ts:
import type { Settings } from 'claude-code'

import { CODE_LOADING_VARIABLES } from './code-loading-variables.js'
import { POLICY_SOURCE_VARIABLES } from './policy-source-variables.js'
import { PROCESS_WRAPPER_VARIABLE } from './process-wrapper-variable.js'

/**
 * The environment variables managed policy sets: every name of its `env`,
 * and the launcher's variable where it names one with `processWrapper`.
 *
 * Always among them: the variables that say where policy is read from,
 * and the ones that can load code into a child the engine starts.
 *
 * @param policy the managed settings, as `$.settings.read` answers them
 * @returns the names, as the policy spells them
 */
export function pinnedNames(policy: Settings): string[] {
  const isWrapped = policy.processWrapper !== undefined

  return [
    ...Object.keys(policy.env ?? {}),
    ...(isWrapped ? [PROCESS_WRAPPER_VARIABLE] : []),
    ...POLICY_SOURCE_VARIABLES,
    ...CODE_LOADING_VARIABLES,
  ]
}

import type { Settings } from 'claude-code'

import Policy from '../policy'
import { serverNameRefusal } from './server-name-refusal.js'
import { TOOL_REGISTER_REFUSAL } from './tool-register-refusal.js'

/**
 * Why managed policy refuses a tool to a plugin a person installed, if it
 * does.
 *
 * Either an MCP allowlist is in force, or the tool would be called by a name
 * that reads as a tool of a server of the organization's.
 *
 * @param policy the managed settings, as `$.settings.read` answers them
 * @param plugin the registering plugin's name
 * @param tool the tool's own name, as the plugin registers it
 * @param id the id the engine recorded for the registering plugin, where
 *           the mod heard its admission
 * @returns the refusal, or undefined when the plugin may add its tool
 */
export const registerRefusalOf = (
  policy: Settings,
  plugin: string,
  tool: string,
  id?: string,
) =>
  Policy.hasMcpAllowlist(policy)
    ? TOOL_REGISTER_REFUSAL
    : Policy.namesOrgTool(policy, plugin, tool, id)
      ? serverNameRefusal(plugin)
      : undefined

files.hooks/held-verdict/verdicts/holds-over.t:
import type { EventResult } from 'claude-code'

import { isSameVerdict } from './is-same-verdict.js'
import Ranking from './ranking'

/**
 * Whether the verdict reached past the user tier holds whole over the
 * chain's answer: a deny, or an ask that names what stands behind it.
 *
 * It holds over a more permissive answer and over the same decision reworded
 * or stripped of what it names; a stricter answer stands. A rule, a hook, a
 * setting, a host or a ceiling counts; the mode's own ask at a dialog never.
 *
 * @param held what the run past the user tier settled on
 * @param answer what the whole chain settled on
 * @returns true when the held verdict is the one to return, as it is
 */
export const holdsOver = (
  held: EventResult<'tool.check'>,
  answer: EventResult<'tool.check'>,
) =>
  !Ranking.isLooser(held, answer) &&
  !isSameVerdict(held, answer) &&
  (held.decision === 'deny' ||
    held.rule !== undefined ||
    held.hook !== undefined ||
    held.setting !== undefined ||
    held.decider !== undefined ||
    held.ceiling !== undefined)
files.hooks/held-verdict/verdicts/is-same-verd:
import type { EventResult } from 'claude-code'

/**
 * Whether two `tool.check` verdicts say the same in every field: decision,
 * reason, and whatever either names (a rule, a hook, a setting, a host).
 *
 * @param one a verdict
 * @param other another, or undefined when nothing settled
 * @returns true when no field differs
 */
export const isSameVerdict = (
  one: EventResult<'tool.check'>,
  other: EventResult<'tool.check'> | undefined,
) =>
  other !== undefined &&
  [one, other]
    .map(verdict =>
      JSON.stringify(
        Object.entries(verdict)
          .filter(([, value]) => value !== undefined)
          .toSorted(([left], [right]) => (left < right ? -1 : 1)),
      ),
    )
    .every((line, _, lines) => line === lines[0])

files.hooks/held-verdict/verdicts/rewritten-by:
import type { TraceEntry } from 'claude-code'

import { isSameVerdict } from './is-same-verdict.js'
import Ranking from './ranking'

/**
 * The links of one run of `tool.check` that may hold a plugin a person
 * installed and that rewrote the verdict handed to them without tightening.
 *
 * A more permissive decision counts, and so does the same decision under
 * another reason, rule or hook. Read off `next.trace`, whose `tier` the
 * engine pins; a batch is named as the engine names it, its members joined.
 *
 * @param trace what settled beneath the hook on its latest `next` call
 * @returns their names, nearest the caller first; none when none rewrote
 */
export const rewrittenByUsers = (
  trace: readonly TraceEntry<'tool.check'>[],
): readonly string[] =>
  trace
    .filter((link, at) => {
      const handed = Ranking.handedTo(trace, at)

      return (
        Ranking.TIERS_HOLDING_USERS.includes(link.tier) &&
        link.returned !== undefined &&
        !Ranking.isLooser(handed, link.returned) &&
        !isSameVerdict(link.returned, handed)
      )
    })
    .map(link => link.plugin)

import type { TraceEntry } from 'claude-code'

/**
 * The verdict handed up to one link of a run: what the nearest link beneath
 * it that settled on anything settled on.
 *
 * Undefined for a link that answered without calling `next`: the trace ends
 * short of the engine there, and nothing beneath it ran.
 *
 * @param trace a run as `next.trace` lists it, nearest the caller first
 * @param at the link's place in that list
 * @returns the verdict, or undefined when nothing settled beneath the link
 */
export const handedTo = (
  trace: readonly TraceEntry<'tool.check'>[],
  at: number,
) => trace.slice(at + 1).find(link => link.returned !== undefined)?.returned
files.hooks/held-verdict/verdicts/ranking/is-l:
import type { EventResult } from 'claude-code'

import { LENIENCY } from './leniency'

/**
 * Whether a link's own verdict is more permissive than the one handed up to
 * it; with nothing handed up (it never called `next`), than a deny.
 *
 * A link that settled on nothing (skipped, rejected) loosened nothing.
 *
 * @param own what the link settled on
 * @param handed what settled beneath it and was handed up, if anything did
 * @returns true when the link loosened the verdict
 */
export const isLooser = (
  own: EventResult<'tool.check'> | undefined,
  handed: EventResult<'tool.check'> | undefined,
) =>
  own !== undefined &&
  LENIENCY[own.decision] > LENIENCY[handed?.decision ?? 'deny']

import type { Settings } from 'claude-code'

import { isServerFileUnreadable } from './is-server-file-unreadable'
import { orgPluginNames } from './org-plugin-names'
import { orgServerNames } from './org-server-names'
import { spellingsOf } from './spellings-of'
import { toolPrefixOf } from './tool-prefix-of'
import { foldedName } from './tool-prefix-of/folded-name'

/**
 * Whether a tool is the organization's: `mcp__<name>__...` for a server its
 * policy names or delivers, and a tool under a seated plugin's name or
 * scope (`plugin_<name>`, which holds its own manifest's servers).
 *
 * A server is told by its name whole, as the engine spells it (spellingsOf),
 * never by a fold: another server whose name only begins like it is not it.
 * A seated plugin is told fold to fold, as the registration check tells it
 * (foldedName), since policy may list its id in another letter case. Where
 * the server file cannot be read, every `mcp__` tool counts.
 *
 * @param policy the managed settings, as `$.settings.read` answers them
 * @param tool the tool's name, as the model sees it
 * @returns true when the tool is the organization's
 */
export const isOrgTool = (policy: Settings, tool: string): boolean =>
  (isServerFileUnreadable(policy) && tool.startsWith('mcp__')) ||
  orgServerNames(policy)
    .flatMap(spellingsOf)
    .some(spelt => tool.startsWith(`mcp__${spelt}__`)) ||
  orgPluginNames(policy)
    .filter(name => foldedName(name) !== '')
    .flatMap(name => [name, `plugin_${name}`])
    .some(owner => `${foldedName(tool)}_`.startsWith(toolPrefixOf(owner)))

import type { Settings } from 'claude-code'

/**
 * Whether the policy read marks the organization's server file
 * (managed-mcp.json) as present and unreadable: its servers cannot be named.
 *
 * @param policy the managed settings, as `$.settings.read` answers them
 * @returns true when the mark is set
 */
export const isServerFileUnreadable = (policy: Settings): boolean =>
  policy.managedMcpServersUnreadable === true

import type { Settings } from 'claude-code'

import { orgPluginNames } from '../org-plugin-names'
import { orgServerNames } from '../org-server-names'

/**
 * Every name whose tools are the organization's: the MCP servers its policy
 * names or delivers, and the plugins it seats itself.
 *
 * Each seated plugin counts twice: by its name, and by its scope
 * (`plugin_<name>`), under which the engine spells the MCP servers the
 * plugin's own manifest declares.
 *
 * @param policy the managed settings, as `$.settings.read` answers them
 * @param own the engine-recorded id of the plugin that asks for itself,
 *            whose own name is left out (orgPluginNames)
 * @returns the names, servers first
 */
export const orgNames = (policy: Settings, own?: string): string[] => [
  ...orgServerNames(policy),
  ...orgPluginNames(policy, own).flatMap(name => [name, `plugin_${name}`]),
]

import { foldedName } from './folded-name'

/**
 * What the folded name of every tool under an MCP server, or of a plugin's
 * own registered tools, begins with: `mcp_<folded name>_`.
 *
 * Compared fold to fold (foldedName), never as written: a name in another
 * case, or with other separators, is the same server to a model.
 *
 * @param name a server's name, or a registering plugin's
 * @returns the folded prefix
 */
export const toolPrefixOf = (name: string) => `mcp_${foldedName(name)}_`

/**
 * A server's or a tool's name as look-alike checks compare it: spelled as
 * the engine spells a name inside a tool's (every other character a `_`,
 * no normalization), lower-cased, runs of `-` and `_` one `_`, trimmed.
 *
 * `Corp__Tools`, `corp-tools` and `corp.tools` all fold to `corp_tools`: a
 * model reads them as one name, so one of them may not pass for another.
 *
 * @param name the name as written
 * @returns the fold
 */
export const foldedName = (name: string) =>
  name
    .replace(/[^a-zA-Z0-9_-]/g, '_')
    .toLowerCase()
    .replace(/[-_]+/g, '_')
    .replace(/^_|_$/g, '')
files.hooks/policy/own-option/member-of/member:
/**
 * One step into settings read as plain data: the value's own member of that
 * name, or undefined when the value is no object or holds none.
 *
 * @param value what was read so far
 * @param key the member's name
 * @returns the member, or undefined
 */
export function memberOf(value: unknown, key: string): unknown {
  const isObject = typeof value === 'object' && value !== null

  return isObject ? new Map(Object.entries(value)).get(key) : undefined
}

/**
 * The tiers a trace entry can carry when a plugin a person installed ran in
 * it: `user`, and `prepend` beneath this plugin's own seat.
 *
 * The engine runs neighbouring plugins that share a worker as one batch and
 * lists the batch under its first member's tier, so an organization's
 * prepended plugin can stand for a batch that holds a person's.
 */
export const TIERS_HOLDING_USERS: readonly unknown[] = Object.freeze([
  'user',
  'prepend',
])

/**
 * A plugin's id as the engine compares ids: NFC, then lower case.
 *
 * A mod imports nothing from the engine, so its rule is copied here; a test
 * in the engine's tree holds the copy equal to it.
 *
 * @param id an id as written, `<name>@<source>`
 * @returns the fold
 */
export const foldedId = (id: string): string =>
  id.normalize('NFC').toLowerCase()

/**
 * Whether an `enabledPlugins` entry turns its plugin on: `true`, or a list
 * of version constraints, as the engine reads one.
 *
 * @param value the entry's value
 * @returns true when the entry turns the plugin on
 */
export const isEnabledEntry = (value: unknown): boolean =>
  value === true || Array.isArray(value)

import type { Settings } from 'claude-code'

import { foldedId } from './folded-id.js'
import { formsOf } from './forms-of.js'
import { isEnabledEntry } from './is-enabled-entry.js'
import { nameOfId } from './name-of-id.js'

/**
 * The names of the plugins the organization itself seats, as their tools
 * are prefixed: an id's name half (nameOfId), in each form the engine may
 * spell it from (formsOf).
 *
 * Those are the ids of prependPlugins and appendPlugins, and every id
 * managed enabledPlugins turns on (isEnabledEntry) but a built-in's, which
 * the engine names.
 *
 * The asking plugin's own id is left out, in every list, exactly when it is
 * one managed enabledPlugins turns on: its name is then its own to use.
 *
 * @param policy the managed settings, as `$.settings.read` answers them
 * @param own the id the engine recorded for the plugin that asks for itself
 *            (`<name>@<source>`), compared as the engine compares ids
 * @returns each such plugin's name, in each form; none where no key names
 *          one
 */
export function orgPluginNames(policy: Settings, own?: string): string[] {
  const enabled = Object.entries(policy.enabledPlugins ?? {}).flatMap(
    ([id, value]) =>
      isEnabledEntry(value) && !id.endsWith('@builtin') ? [id] : [],
  )
  const isOwn = (id: string) =>
    typeof own === 'string' && foldedId(id) === foldedId(own)
  const isExempt = enabled.some(isOwn)

  return [policy.prependPlugins, policy.appendPlugins, enabled].flatMap(
    (listed: unknown) =>
      (Array.isArray(listed) ? listed : []).flatMap((id: unknown) => {
        const name = typeof id === 'string' ? nameOfId(id) : ''
        const isLeftOut = typeof id === 'string' && isExempt && isOwn(id)

        return name !== '' && !isLeftOut ? formsOf(name) : []
      }),
  )
}
